source: Ichien, Stamenkovic, Holyoak (2023) Large language model displays emergent ability to interpret novel literary metaphors (Study 1, Fig-QA)
finding: Zero-shot GPT-4 nearly matched humans on the Fig-QA metaphor paraphrase choice task.
numbers: 1,146 test metaphors. Human 94.42% (95.39% when confident). GPT-4 zero-shot 91.27%. GPT-3 Davinci zero-shot 68.41%. Fine-tuned RoBERTa 90.32% (8,016 training metaphors). GPT-4 said 'neither' on 3.35% of items, counted as wrong.
limits: Fig-QA metaphors are mostly common ones that may be in training data. GPT-3 was scored by plausibility, GPT-4 by direct question.
agent_relevance: Frontier models read metaphors well in forced choice. Comprehension of a restated metaphor is unlikely to be the weak step in O6; choosing and applying the source domain is.

source: Ichien, Stamenkovic, Holyoak (2023) Large language model displays emergent ability to interpret novel literary metaphors (Study 2, Serbian poets' metaphors)
finding: On novel literary metaphors by Serbian poets (translated), GPT-4 interpretations were rated by blind human judges as better than those of every human participant. For reversed metaphors GPT-4 restored the canonical meaning like people.
numbers: Human participants were US college students. Reversed-metaphor items: GPT-4 restored canonical meaning 56% of the time, humans 50%; item-level point-biserial r=0.79, p<.001 over 55 reversed metaphors.
limits: Human baseline was students, not poets or critics. Some translated lines may have been online before 2022.
agent_relevance: Models share the human habit of repairing reversed mappings. State the direction (target is the source) explicitly in any scaffold.

source: Ichien, Stamenkovic, Holyoak (2023) Large language model displays emergent ability to interpret novel literary metaphors (Study 3, English poems)
finding: GPT-4 gave accurate interpretations of novel English poems per a human critic, but the critic judged GPT-4's own poems harshly.
numbers: Interpretations judged highly accurate by all authors; generated poems called scathing (no counts reported).
limits: Small qualitative evaluation with one critic.
agent_relevance: Comprehension runs ahead of generation. Let the model read mappings; verify the ones it invents.

source: Prystawski, Thibodeau, Potts, Goodman (2022) Psychologically-informed chain-of-thought prompts for metaphor understanding in LLMs (DaVinci)
finding: On a four-way paraphrase choice for Katz-corpus metaphors, GPT-3 DaVinci scored high with plain 10-shot answers; the type of rationale made little difference.
numbers: 150 test metaphors (125 non-literary, 25 literary). Mean appropriateness 1-4, random 2.5. DaVinci: options only 2.73; no rationale 3.71; non-explanation 3.58; subject-object 3.84; question-under-discussion (QUD) 3.74; similarity 3.68. 95% CIs about +/-0.1.
limits: Temperature 0.2, 10-shot prompts. Differences among rationale types are within overlapping intervals. Strong model near ceiling.
agent_relevance: An explicit mapping step added no clear value for comprehension in a strong model. Do not assume it helps by default.

source: Prystawski, Thibodeau, Potts, Goodman (2022) Psychologically-informed chain-of-thought prompts for metaphor understanding in LLMs (Curie)
finding: The smaller GPT-3 Curie was at chance without rationales and rose above chance only with QUD or similarity rationales.
numbers: Curie: no rationale 2.49; QUD 2.76 (p=.005 vs chance); similarity 2.72 (p=.02); subject-object 2.63 and options-only 2.52 not different from chance. QUD vs no rationale beta=.41 [-.02,.84], not significant. Unparseable answers: 47 of 150 with subject-object prompts.
limits: One model family, 2022 models.
agent_relevance: Scaffold gains depend on base model strength: structure helps weak models more than strong ones.

source: Prystawski, Thibodeau, Potts, Goodman (2022) Psychologically-informed chain-of-thought prompts for metaphor understanding in LLMs (design: familiarity check)
finding: Authors compared performance across metaphor familiarity (published human norms) to separate memorised from reasoned answers.
numbers: Corpus 280 metaphors (230 non-literary, 50 literary), split 30 train / 100 dev / 150 test; 4 hand-written paraphrases per item scored 1-4.
limits: Only 'X is Y' metaphors.
agent_relevance: Good pattern for our evals: check that a gain survives on unfamiliar items.

source: Tong, Choenni, Lewis, Shutova (2024) Metaphor Understanding Challenge Dataset (MUNCH) (paraphrase judgement)
finding: With inapt paraphrases as controls, LLaMA-13B, LLaMA-30B and GPT-3.5 (text-davinci-003) were mostly below the 0.25 chance level at picking the apt paraphrase.
numbers: Mean accuracy over 3 prompts, 4 choices (chance .25). Word-judgement implicit: LLaMA-13B .28, LLaMA-30B .21, GPT-3.5 .23. Metaphor-Word variants: .30/.19/.20. Dataset: over 10k apt and 1.5k inapt paraphrases across 4 genres.
limits: Old models only (no GPT-4 or Llama-2). Large prompt variance for LLaMA-13B.
agent_relevance: Earlier success on metaphor tasks may come from lexical similarity. Add inapt-paraphrase controls when testing O6.

source: Tong, Choenni, Lewis, Shutova (2024) Metaphor Understanding Challenge Dataset (MUNCH) (generation, prompt effects)
finding: In free paraphrase generation GPT-3.5 matched human words best; telling the model which word is metaphorical helped LLaMA-13B.
numbers: Mean MRR over 3 prompts: LLaMA-30B .33, GPT-3.5 .47. Recall@5: .22 vs .28. Recall@10 LLaMA-30B .33. Naming the metaphorical word raised LLaMA-13B word-judgement accuracy.
limits: Human paraphrases are the gold standard; all models preferred different answers than humans.
agent_relevance: Flag the figurative phrase before restating. Cheap scaffold for O6.

source: Liu, Cui, Zheng, Neubig (2022) Testing the Ability of Language Models to Interpret Figurative Language (Fig-QA) (accuracy by model)
finding: Zero-shot GPT-3 Davinci reached 68.41% on Winograd-style metaphor interpretation; humans 94.42%. Accuracy rose steadily with model size.
numbers: Zero-shot: GPT-2 53.93; GPT-neo 1.3B 56.89; GPT-3 Ada 62.91; Babbage 65.35; Davinci 68.41. Fine-tuned RoBERTa 90.32, BERT 85.69 (best splits). Human 94.42 (10 volunteers).
limits: Paired scoring (both versions of a metaphor correct) cut model accuracy sharply while humans were least affected.
agent_relevance: Pair-consistency checks expose shallow success; use them to test mapping reasoning.

source: Liu, Cui, Zheng, Neubig (2022) Testing the Ability of Language Models to Interpret Figurative Language (Fig-QA) (generation and error types)
finding: When asked to complete the meaning of a metaphor, GPT-3 often restated it or contradicted itself across samples.
numbers: GPT-3 Davinci completions: 50.8% correct counting restated 'literal' answers as wrong; 63.9% not counting them. In 37.7% of cases the 4 completions contradicted each other. At least one correct for 78.1% of phrases; all 4 correct for only 19.3%. Krippendorff alpha .5567.
limits: Three authors labelled; moderate agreement.
agent_relevance: Single-draw metaphor readings are unreliable. Sample several and keep the consistent reading.

source: Liu, Cui, Zheng, Neubig (2022) Testing the Ability of Language Models to Interpret Figurative Language (Fig-QA) (knowledge categories)
finding: Test items were tagged by knowledge needed. Object common sense was needed in 68.35% of the test set, visual 14.73%, social 27.55%, cultural 16.56% (US-centred).
numbers: Per-category model accuracies are in the paper's table but were scrambled in the extracted text, so not recorded.
limits: Categories overlap; tagged by three authors.
agent_relevance: Source domains drawn from physical objects are the bulk of the test; that is the CMT core.

source: Aghazadeh, Fayyaz, Yaghoobzadeh (2022) Metaphors in Pre-Trained Language Models: Probing and Generalization Across Datasets and Languages
finding: Probing shows pretrained LMs encode metaphoricity, mostly in middle layers, and it transfers across English, Spanish, Russian and Farsi and across datasets when annotation style matches.
numbers: Edge probing and MDL probing on several detection datasets (for example VUA Verbs 9,176 / 1,310 / 2,622 train/dev/test); chance 50%.
limits: Detecting a metaphor is not the same as naming its source domain; transfer drops when annotation guidelines differ.
agent_relevance: Metaphor information sits in internal states, so prompting can elicit it; a detector alone does not give a usable source domain.

source: Wachowiak and Gromann (2023) Does GPT-3 Grasp Metaphors? Identifying Metaphor Mappings with Generative Language Models (few-shot source domain)
finding: Given a sentence and target domain, GPT-3 (davinci-002) with 12 few-shot examples named the correct source domain far more often on a curated list than on realistic text, and worse in Spanish.
numbers: Manual accuracy: Metaphor List 81.33%; LCC English 53.74%; LCC Spanish 34.65%; non-metaphoric items called non-metaphoric 42.11%; sample-weighted average 60.22% (unweighted 52.96%). Best prompt had 12 examples; high variance across example sets.
limits: Two authors as annotators, kappa about .51 (moderate). 12 LCC sentences dropped for faulty gold labels. Old model.
agent_relevance: Direct test of the CMT core step: only about half correct on real text. Source choice needs a check.

source: Wachowiak and Gromann (2023) Does GPT-3 Grasp Metaphors? Identifying Metaphor Mappings with Generative Language Models (errors, fine-tuning)
finding: Most common error was a hallucinated source domain with no cue in the sentence. Fine-tuning reduced the variety of source domains produced.
numbers: Spanish errors: 62.12% were non-metaphoric calls for items that should be metaphoric; 19.70% wrong source. Example: 'China is a fertile ground for revolt' gold PLANTS, model LAND. Largest model davinci-002 clearly beat smaller ones and a fine-tuned GPT-3.
limits: Qualitative error typology by the authors.
agent_relevance: In O6 require the agent to quote the words in the problem that support the chosen source domain.

source: Stowe, Ribeiro, Gurevych (2021) Metaphor Generation with Conceptual Mappings (CM-Lex, CM-BART)
finding: Encoding source/target domain pairs (FrameNet-based) into a generator controls metaphors better than unconstrained systems.
numbers: CM-BART beat all systems on metaphoricity by about 7% and domain evocation by about 33%; CM-Lex beat neural baselines on domain evocation by about 13%. Exact match to gold: CM-BART 29.3% vs MetMask 8.7%, MERMAID 13.3%, CM-Lex 10.7%.
limits: Human annotator agreement was low: Krippendorff alpha .50 metaphoricity, .37 source domain (3 experts, 100 sentences). Verbs only.
agent_relevance: An older system built on CMT: a conceptual mapping used as a control signal works for generation.

source: Stowe, Ribeiro, Gurevych (2021) Metaphor Generation with Conceptual Mappings (rare and unseen mappings)
finding: For rare and unseen mappings CM-BART still beat CM-Lex, but outputs became inconsistent when source and target domains were too incongruent.
numbers: Example: framing operating a vehicle as DEATH gave 'die' (CM-BART) and 'fell' (CM-Lex). Per-cell human scores were scrambled in the extracted text, not recorded.
limits: Qualitative examples.
agent_relevance: Some source domains do not fit a target. The agent should drop a source that produces incoherent mappings.

source: Webb, Holyoak, Lu (2023) Emergent analogical reasoning in large language models. Nature Human Behaviour (matrix and letter strings)
finding: Zero-shot GPT-3 matched or beat UCLA undergraduates on text matrix reasoning and letter-string analogies, with similar error patterns.
numbers: Digit matrices: humans N=40, GPT-3 above mean, odds ratio 1.88, p=.005, CI [1.21,2.91]. Letter strings: humans N=57, GPT-3 OR 1.76, p=6.3e-5, error-pattern correlation r(39)=0.7.
limits: Students as human baseline. GPT-4 tested only informally (better on story analogies).
agent_relevance: Models can map relations zero-shot. Generality is the open question (see c19).

source: Webb, Holyoak, Lu (2023) Emergent analogical reasoning in large language models. Nature Human Behaviour (verbal and story analogies)
finding: GPT-3 preferred higher-order relational matches in stories like humans, and semantically distant analogies hurt both.
numbers: Story analogies: N=54 humans. Verbal analogies: UCLA test, Sternberg-Nigro, SAT items (GPT-3 above estimated high-school SAT average). Distance effect on Jones et al. set: OR=3.24, p=.0165, CI [1.24,8.5].
limits: Some tasks hand built; SAT item contamination possible.
agent_relevance: Supports restating via a relational source; far sources cost accuracy.

source: Lewis and Mitchell (2024) Using Counterfactual Tasks to Evaluate the Generality of Analogical Reasoning in LLMs
finding: On letter-string analogies with permuted or symbol alphabets, humans stayed high while GPT-3, 3.5 and 4 dropped sharply.
numbers: Mean accuracy over all counterfactual alphabets: humans 0.753 [0.734,0.773] (1,876 samples); the three GPT models between 0.350 and 0.488 (6,840 samples each; model-to-row order scrambled in the PDF text). Counterfactual comprehension checks mostly 0.9+ for GPT-4, so the fault is not only misunderstanding the new alphabet.
limits: One analogy domain; temperature 0.
agent_relevance: Restating in a source domain may only work when the source looks like training data. Test unfamiliar sources.

source: Czinczoll, Yannakoudakis, Mishra, Shutova (2022) Scientific and Creative Analogies in Pretrained Language Models (SCAN)
finding: On SCAN, a set of systematic mappings between dissimilar domains including conceptual metaphors, GPT-2 and BERT scored very low.
numbers: Zero-shot MRR: GPT-2 .022 on SCAN vs .099 on BATS; BERT .048 on SCAN vs .121 on BATS; GloVe last on SCAN. Models did better on scientific analogies than on metaphors. One example sentence did not help; training on BATS made SCAN worse.
limits: Small old models; no GPT-3 or instruction-tuned models tested.
agent_relevance: Cross-domain mappings including metaphors were hard for 2022 models. Re-test with current models before relying on it.

source: Zheng et al. (2023) Take a Step Back: Evoking Reasoning via Abstraction in LLMs
finding: Asking the model to first state a higher-level principle improved hard reasoning tasks. This is a re-representation move close to O6.
numbers: PaLM-2L: MMLU Physics 66.4 -> 73.2, Chemistry 70.9 -> 81.8, TimeQA 41.5 -> 66.0 (68.7 with RAG), MuSiQue 42.8 best, StrategyQA 86.4 best. GPT-4 Physics 69.4 -> 84.5 but CoT alone gave 82.9. Fixes 20.5% of baseline errors, adds 11.9%.
limits: Gain shrinks on GPT-4 where CoT is strong. Most remaining errors come from reasoning, not from abstraction.
agent_relevance: Abstraction-first is cheap and measurable. Use as a baseline against our O6.

source: Yasunaga et al. (2024) Large Language Models as Analogical Reasoners (ICLR)
finding: Asking the model to recall its own related problems before solving beat 0-shot and few-shot CoT without labelled examples.
numbers: GPT-3.5-turbo: GSM8K 5-shot CoT 75.0 -> 77.8 with diverse self-generated exemplars (non-diverse 75.9); MATH 33.0 -> 37.3. Codeforces Acc@1 GPT-3.5 15% vs GPT-4 16%. Manual check of 50 failures: 28 had relevant correct exemplars but still failed, 12 had wrong exemplar solutions, 10 irrelevant.
limits: Analogs are same-domain problems, not cross-domain metaphors.
agent_relevance: Self-generated analogs help, but a good analog does not guarantee a solution. Add verification.

source: Yu, He, Ying (2024) Thought Propagation: An Analogical Approach to Complex Reasoning with LLMs (ICLR)
finding: A loop that proposes and solves analogous problems, then reuses their solutions, improved three task types.
numbers: Average +12% absolute in finding optimal shortest paths, +13% human preference in creative writing, +15% task completion in LLM-agent planning.
limits: Analogs are same-structure variants. Numbers are from the abstract.
agent_relevance: Closest published agent-loop use of analogy. Reuse of solved analogs works inside a loop.

source: Chakrabarty et al. (2023) I Spy a Metaphor: LLMs and Diffusion Models Co-Create Visual Metaphors
finding: Chain-of-thought elaboration of the source image by GPT-3 raised image quality for visual metaphors; humans still edited 29% of elaborations.
numbers: Dataset 6,476 visual metaphors for 1,540 linguistic metaphors. Illustrators preferred human-AI images 45% vs LLM-DALL-E 2 18% (37% tie). Perfect: 63.6% vs 52%. Fine-tuning OFA on it raised visual-entailment accuracy 23 points. Fleiss kappa .57.
limits: Failures: dropped 'moonless', missed shadows.
agent_relevance: Spelling out implicit meaning plus concrete objects of the source is a prompt recipe that works.

source: Kabra, Liu, Khanuja et al. (2023) Multi-lingual and Multi-cultural Figurative Language Understanding (MABL)
finding: Figurative inference in seven non-English languages was weaker than English, and figurative vocabulary depends on culture.
numbers: XLM-R large overall 63.99%, culturally specific items 61.68%. Smallest model (mBERT) under 60% for all languages. Translate-to-English helped some languages (sw, yo, kn) by 7 to 17 points; Indonesian zero-shot already about 83.6% of English performance in XLM-R. Table columns partly scrambled.
limits: Mid-size multilingual encoders, not chat models.
agent_relevance: Mappings like UP is GOOD are not universal. Do not assume a source domain transfers across user cultures.

source: Dodge et al. (2015) MetaNet; Mohler et al. (2014); Shaikh et al. (2014) (as cited in Stowe et al. 2021)
finding: Earlier AI systems built conceptual-metaphor repositories from frame lexicons (MetaNet), found source domains with vector spaces, and built rule-based conceptual spaces.
numbers: None read this session.
limits: Known only from the Stowe et al. related-work paragraph.
agent_relevance: Prior art for a source-domain lexicon an agent could query.

source: Mitchell (2020) Can GPT-3 make analogies? (as cited in Czinczoll et al. 2022)
finding: Blog report that GPT-3 benefited from a worked example in analogy tasks; Czinczoll found no benefit from one example for GPT-2 and BERT.
numbers: Not read.
limits: Secondhand.
agent_relevance: A worked mapping in the prompt may help only larger models.
